summary: Berkeley County, SC tower first erected in the 1930s at Bethera, moved to Witherbee in 1952 and used by the Forest Service until 1989; a news story says it still stands.

facts.design: 100' LS-40 Aermotor steel tower with 7' x 7' metal cab; original design and materials retained
facts.status_note: Undated news story says it still stands; no later condition report found

access.note: Tower sits on a Forest Service site (Witherbee station); no public access listing found

visit.trail_note: No public visit route found; the tower stands on a Forest Service site, so ask the Francis Marion ranger district before going

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower moved to the Witherbee Ranger Station; the news story says the Witherbee Ranger District Office. Both describe the same Forest Service site, so the story uses both names.

notes_for_editor: Register, the Former Fire Lookout Sites Bethera entry, and an undated news story cover the history. Current status rests only on the undated news story ('still standing'). The 2024 NEPA page covers two administrative buildings and does not name the tower. Built year 1930 is a decade placeholder for the 1930s. OSM node 357111662 (ele 15) was read but not cited. A current photo or ranger-district check would firm up status before publication.
